items.title: Movement of tourists increases by 254 percent
items.summary: Maputo, 06 Nov (AIM) – The Mozambican President Daniel Chapo has revealed that the movement of tourists and investors arriving in the country increased by 254 percent this year, when compared to the same period in 2025. According to Chapo, speaking at the opening of the second edition of the Mozambique Tourism Summit, in Vilankulo, southern province of Inhambane, the growth is the result of reforms introduced to boost the tourism sector. “The results stem from measures introduced in recent months to facilitate the entry of visitors and attract investment, including the implementation of an electronic visa platform and the creation of the so-called “Visa Gold”, designed to attract foreign investors”, he said. The President highlighted the creation of the National Agency for Tourism Development and Investment (Anditur), which replaced the former National Tourism Institute (Inatur), as well as the Southern Corridor Special Tourism Economic Zone, which incorporates the destinations of Vilankulo, Pomene and Inhassoro, all in Inhambane province.

items.title: Number of detainees in connection with bishop’s murder rises to five
items.summary: Maputo, 06 Nov (AIM) – The number of suspects detained in connection with the murder of Osório Citora Afonso, Bishop of the Diocese of Quelimane, in the central Mozambican province of Zambézia, has risen from four to five. Bishop Osório Afonso, who was also Apostolic Administrator of the Archdiocese of Beira, in the central province of Sofala, was shot dead last June with an AKM-type firearm. Among the suspects, there are two Catholic priests, a guard employed by the Quelimane Diocese and two civilians. According Fred Jamal, Chief Prosecutor Zambezia Province, speaking to reports, on Thursday, as part of Legal Awareness Day, investigations are underway, especially to identify the perpetrators who physically carried out the murder. “Fortunately, the extension of the preventive detention period gives us more time to carry out our work properly, since it has been extended to 12 months. Work is underway to identify the material perpetrators.

items.title: European shares join a global sell-off as AI spending fears rattle Wall Street and Asian markets
items.summary: European shares have fallen after sharp losses in Asia and on Wall Street. Doubts over huge AI investments and fears of curbs following the Democrats' US midterm victory have rattled global markets European shares fell sharply in early trading on Friday as a global sell-off fueled by concerns over artificial intelligence stocks spread from Wall Street to Asia and Europe Fears of curbs on AI data-center spending have added to investors' concerns after Democrats won control of both chambers of the US Congress The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 1.6% in early trading, wiping out its gains for the week.

items.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
items.summary: President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud unlawfully extended his term, escalating a political crisis and a standoff between the presidency and judiciary Thursday's ruling came a day after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed - a move which the court said the president lacked the authority to take The court also ordered political leaders to agree on an electoral plan within 30 days and hold elections within 90 days, potentially disrupting government plans for nationwide polls next year Mohamud's four-year mandate expired in May, but his administration extended it by a year through law changes approved by parliament in March Opposition groups accuse him of using the constitutional changes to prolong his rule But the president insists the reforms are necessary to move Somalia towards fully democratic elections, replacing the clan-based system in which elders pick their representatives Somalia last held nationwide direct elections in 1969 and has been wracked by civil war for…

items.title: Germany news: Trial of alleged 'Reichsbürger' group ringleaders begins
items.summary: Four members of the banned far-right "Kingdom of Germany" are on trial for belonging to a criminal organization. Meanwhile, a new study warns data centers could lead to water stress in Germany. Follow DW for more Read below for the top headlines from across Germany on Friday, November 6: Residents in the western city of Krefeld woke to warning sirens in the early hours after a truck accident nearby caused a nitric acid leak About 200 firefighters worked at the scene for most of the morning to contain the leak The truck was reportedly carrying 23 metric tons of highly corrosive acid when it crashed and overturned at around 3 a.m. local time (0200 GMT) on Highway 57 Authorities had warned of an "extreme danger" within a 1-kilometer (0.6-mile) radius of the site and urged residents in that area to stay indoors and keep their windows closed "Most of the spilled nitric acid has now been contained," emergency responders reported.

items.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
items.summary: Au was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state" Macau has sentenced an ex-lawmaker and pro-democracy campaigner to 12 years and six months' jail in the city's first national security case Following a closed-door trial, Au Kam San, 69, was convicted on Friday of "subversion against the political power of the state", among other offences His wife Virginia Cheang condemned the ruling, calling the case a "groundless persecution designed to humiliate Au" Macau was handed back to China in 1999, ending over 400 years of Portuguese administration.
